title: arXiv Mathematics — 16 November 2026 batch: eight notable new papers
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This ordering is inferred from qualitative attention signals and mathematical significance; citation evidence is limited for this very recent batch, so it is a notable-recent-papers list, not a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
sections.abstract: The authors embed every compact finite-rank nilspace into a toral nilspace and use this to prove the Jamneshan–Tao conjecture, obtaining a Gowers-norm inverse theorem for second-countable compact abelian groups with nilmanifold correlators.
sections.claimed_result: Every compact finite-rank k-step nilspace embeds continuously into a k-step toral nilspace. For each k and δ, a 1-bounded Borel function on a second-countable compact Hausdorff abelian group with U^(k+1) norm at least δ correlates by at least ε(k,δ) with a bounded-Lipschitz function pulled back from one of a finite family of connected filtered nilmanifolds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: k≥1, 0<δ≤1; second-countable compact Hausdorff abelian groups and 1-bounded Borel functions; target family and constants depend on k and δ.
sections.unique_caveat: Builds on the general nilspace inverse theorem and prior nilspace structure results; the conclusion is not an inverse theorem for arbitrary non-abelian groups.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An independent Post-Cutoff research explainer discusses the conjecture’s resolution; the paper is cross-listed in group theory, combinatorics, and dynamics and states a concrete structural theorem.

sections.title: The four-dimensional Borsuk number is five or six
sections.abstract: For every bounded subset of R^4 with positive diameter, the author proves a partition into at most six sets of smaller diameter, improving the previous upper bound of seven; the theorem is formalized in Lean.
sections.claimed_result: Every bounded positive-diameter subset of R^4 partitions into at most six smaller-diameter parts. A regular 4-simplex requires five, so the Borsuk number b4 is either five or six.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Arbitrary bounded subsets of four-dimensional Euclidean space with positive diameter; no convexity assumption is stated in the theorem.
sections.unique_caveat: The exact value remains unresolved: this proves 5≤b4≤6, not whether five always suffice. Lean formalization is a checked proof artifact, not independent peer review.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It improves a recent upper bound from seven to six and the main theorem is formalized in Lean 4.

sections.title: Sharp Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced Axisymmetric Euler Without Swirl via Multiscale Data
sections.abstract: The authors construct compactly supported vorticity for an unforced axisymmetric Euler flow without swirl that blows up in finite time, with initial vorticity in every Hölder class C^α for α<1/3 simultaneously.
sections.claimed_result: They construct a divergence-free axisymmetric velocity without swirl, with compactly supported vorticity and initial velocity in L² and C^{1,α} for every α<1/3, smooth away from the origin, whose classical solution loses regularity in finite time. The initial vorticity is simultaneously in all C^α, α<1/3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Unforced incompressible Euler in R^3, axisymmetry, no swirl, and rough data strictly below the known global-regularity threshold α=1/3.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction is not from smooth initial data and does not settle the smooth-data blow-up problem, particularly in the axisymmetric-with-swirl setting.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors give a sharp-threshold construction, simultaneous subcritical regularity, and a specific multiscale cascade mechanism.

sections.title: The roads taken in the directed landscape
sections.abstract: Almost surely, every finite-landscape-length path spends all but a set of times of Hausdorff dimension at most 57/61 on interiors of geodesics; the authors also construct paths with exceptional-time dimension at least 1/3.
sections.claimed_result: For G, the union of interiors of all directed-landscape geodesics, almost surely every finite-length path lies in G except on a time set of Hausdorff dimension at most 57/61; they also exhibit finite-length paths with exceptional set dimension at least 1/3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The random directed landscape, almost-surely; the upper bound applies to every finite-landscape-length path in a realization.
sections.unique_caveat: The upper and lower exceptional-set bounds leave a substantial gap; the abstract does not claim 57/61 is sharp.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result has an independent Fields Institute talk listing and a University of Toronto mathematics-seminar listing, as well as a quantitative almost-sure theorem.

sections.title: Smale's mean value constant (1981) equals 4
sections.abstract: For the extremal quantity K(d) defined from critical values of normalized complex polynomials of degree d, the author proves sup_d K(d)=4 and K(d) tends to 4 as d tends to infinity; the main theorem is also formalized in Lean 4.
sections.claimed_result: For complex polynomials p of degree d≥2 with p(0)=0 and p′(0)≠0, define S(p)=min_c |p(c)/(c p′(0))| over critical points c and K(d)=sup_p S(p). The author proves sup_d K(d)=4 and K(d)→4.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The supremum defining K(d) is over normalized complex polynomials as stated in the abstract; the result concerns the degree-varying supremum and its limit.
sections.unique_caveat: Every individual K(d) is strictly below 4, so no fixed degree attains the supremum; exact K(d) for each finite degree is not given in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It resolves the value of a classical constant and links an explicit construction with a Lean 4 proof artifact; a public mathematics account also mentioned the result.

sections.title: No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3)
sections.abstract: The authors answer Dean’s problem by proving that no free lattice contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of sublattices isomorphic to the free lattice on three generators; the theorem is checked in Agda.
sections.claimed_result: No free lattice contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of copies of FL(3); without requiring the links to be free, FL(3) does contain an infinite ascending chain of 3-generated sublattices.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Free lattices over generator sets with decidable equality for the stated Agda formalization; the theorem is claimed for free lattices and the proof is checked under Agda’s safe flags.
sections.unique_caveat: The chain prohibition depends on each link being isomorphic to FL(3); it does not imply stabilization for arbitrary 3-generated sublattices, which the paper shows can fail.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It answers Dean’s problem, is cross-listed across algebra and logic, and has a public Agda formalization.

sections.title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
sections.abstract: For every sufficiently large odd s, the authors prove that at least 2.78√(s log log s / log s) among ζ(3), ζ(5), …, ζ(s) are irrational, improving the previous estimate by a factor involving √(log log s).
sections.claimed_result: For all sufficiently large odd integers s, at least 2.78√(s log log s / log s) of ζ(3), ζ(5), …, ζ(s) are irrational.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: An asymptotic lower bound for sufficiently large odd s; the abstract gives no explicit threshold.
sections.unique_caveat: It bounds the number of irrational values but does not identify which individual ζ(2k+1) are irrational or prove all odd zeta values irrational.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It improves a quantitative irrationality bound and cross-lists number theory, analysis, and combinatorics; the abstract identifies the combined proof ingredients.

sections.title: Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group
sections.abstract: The authors claim that every tracial ultraproduct of complex matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group, implying uncountably many nonisomorphic matrix ultraproducts and answering a question of Sorin Popa.
sections.claimed_result: Every tracial ultraproduct of matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group and, more strongly, trivial first-order fundamental group; the authors infer that there are uncountably many nonisomorphic such ultraproducts.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Tracial ultraproducts of complex matrix algebras; the abstract does not further specify the ultrafilter or matrix-size sequence.
sections.unique_caveat: The arXiv comment calls this a first draft and invites comments; treat the strong classification claim as a preprint result pending expert scrutiny.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It states a concrete operator-algebra result answering a question of Popa and proves a stronger first-order version, with cross-listing in logic and representation theory.
